text: What I mean by low company, which should by all means be avoided, is the company of those, who, absolutely insignificant and contemptible in themselves, think they are honored by being in your company; and who flatter every vice and every folly you have, in order to engage you to converse with them.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XVI, to his son, London, October 9, Old Style 1747
